title: sedum douglasii subsp. ciliosum
intro: Sedum douglasii subsp. ciliosum, commonly known as Douglas' sedum or cliff stonecrop, is a subspecies of succulent plant that belongs to the Crassulaceae family. It is native to the western coast of North America and has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, offering various health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which can help to soothe skin irritations, wounds, and promote overall well-being. The therapeutic actions of Sedum douglasii subsp. ciliosum include its antimicrobial, antifungal, and antiseptic properties, making it effective in treating infections, wounds, and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, terpenoids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been shown to exhibit potential anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities.
